Lead Story

Harbor Crossing Project Reaches Its Final Span

By Communications Team · November 23, 2026

After 31 months of design, fabrication and construction, the last steel girder of the Harbor Crossing pedestrian and transit bridge was lifted into place on November 12. The milestone marks the completion of the structural phase of the largest project in Northbridge history, delivered by a joint team of more than 60 structural, geotechnical, and construction-management engineers.

“Every discipline in this firm touched this bridge. Seeing the final span settle into place was a proud moment for all of us.” — Dana Whitfield, Project Director

The team overcame significant challenges along the way, including complex tidal-zone foundations and a redesign of the main span to cut embodied carbon by 18%. Finishing work, instrumentation, and load testing will continue through the first quarter of 2027, with the opening ceremony planned for spring.

Leadership extends sincere thanks to everyone involved, and to the families who supported long field days and late nights. A celebration for the project team is scheduled for December (see Upcoming Events below).

Employee Spotlight

PN

Priya Nair, P.E.

Senior Geotechnical Engineer · Boston Office · 9 years at Northbridge

What are you working on? I led the foundation design for the Harbor Crossing piers. Designing for tidal soils is part science, part patience.

Proudest moment? Watching the first pier cap get poured exactly on schedule after months of modeling.

Advice for new engineers? Visit the site early and often. No model replaces standing in the soil you're designing for.

Outside of work? Trail running, and she is training for her first ultramarathon in May.
